facts.text: Xiaoliuqiu (Liuqiu) is a small coral island in southwestern Taiwan, off Pingtung County; the boat trip from Donggang takes about 30 minutes.
Visitors to the island may see green sea turtles or even swim with them.
Since fishing nets were banned there, the island's green sea turtle population has grown in recent years.
The Ocean Conservation Administration's monthly drone surveys recorded an average of 637 sea turtles per month around the island in 2023.
Green turtles are named for the color of their fat, not their shells; adults mainly eat seaweed (algae) and sea grass.
Green turtles nest on Xiaoliuqiu's beaches; the nesting season runs from May to October.
TurtleSpot Taiwan, a citizen science project started in 2017, asks divers and other ocean lovers to report turtle sightings with photos.
The shape, size and arrangement of the scales around a sea turtle's eyes and on its face are unique to each turtle, like human fingerprints, so photos can identify individuals.
Identifying individual turtles helps researchers learn where turtles live and move, check whether injured turtles recover after release, and study threats such as fishing gear.
Sea turtles are protected wildlife in Taiwan; visitors are told not to touch, chase, disturb or feed them.
Disturbing protected sea turtles can lead to up to one year in prison or a fine of up to NT$300,000.
A local group, the Taiwan Loo-Koo Yu Association, removes trash from beaches so that turtles can lay eggs.
Xiaoliuqiu is described as one of Taiwan's best-known habitats for sea turtles.
